claim_judgments.rationale: Accurately reflects the requirement in subsection (a)(1) that the chief executive officer of a State seeking a grant or allotment designate a lead agency complying with paragraph (2) in the State application submitted under subsection (b).
Correctly captures the lead agency duty under subsection (a)(2)(A) to develop the State plan for submission to the Secretary under subsection (b).

Faithfully reflects subsection (a)(2)(B) requiring the lead agency to hold at least one public hearing with sufficient time and statewide notice regarding the proposed use and distribution of grant or allotment funds.
Faithfully captures the lead agency duty under subsection (a)(2)(C) to conduct reviews of eligible entities under section 9914.
Accurately reflects subsection (a)(3) requiring the State to hold at least one legislative hearing every 3 years in conjunction with State plan development to maintain eligibility.

Faithfully reflects the general application and plan submission requirement under subsection (b), including the effective starting point (fiscal year 2000), plan period (1 to 2 fiscal years), and 30-day pre-fiscal year submission deadline.
Accurately combines the assurance and descriptive requirements of subsection (b)(1)(A)(i)-(vii) assisting low-income individuals and families across the specified domains.
Correctly captures the plan assurance requirement in subsection (b)(1)(B) addressing the needs of youth in low-income communities through youth development programs.
Correctly reflects subsection (b)(1)(C) requiring plan assurances regarding coordinating with and making effective use of other related programs, including State welfare reform.
Faithfully reflects subsection (b)(2) requiring a description of how the State intends to use discretionary funds from the remainder of the grant or allotment described in section 9907(b).
Accurately groups the information items required under subsection (b)(3)(A)-(D) provided by eligible entities regarding service delivery, linkages, resource coordination, and innovative initiatives.
Faithfully reflects subsection (b)(4) requiring an assurance that eligible entities will provide emergency supplies, services, and nutritious food to counteract starvation and malnutrition.
Correctly reflects subsection (b)(5) requiring an assurance of service coordination/linkages to prevent duplication and a description of employment and training activity coordination under WIOA.
Faithfully reflects subsection (b)(6) requiring assurances of antipoverty program coordination and conduct of emergency energy crisis intervention programs where appropriate.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(7) requiring an assurance that the State will permit and cooperate with Federal investigations under section 9916.

Accurately reflects subsection (b)(8) requiring an assurance protecting previously funded eligible entities from termination or proportional reduction without cause, notice, and a hearing on the record.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(9) requiring an assurance regarding coordination and partnership with other organizations serving low-income residents to the maximum extent possible.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(10) requiring an assurance that eligible entities establish procedures for petitioning for adequate board representation.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(11) requiring an assurance that the State secure community action plans with community-needs assessments from eligible entities as a condition of funding.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(12) requiring assurances of participation in ROMA or an alternative system by fiscal year 2001 and description of outcome measures.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(13) requiring the plan to contain information describing how the State will carry out the assurances in subsection (b).
Faithfully defines 'cause' for a funding reduction under subsection (c)(1), covering both statewide redistribution circumstances and compliance/performance failures.
Faithfully defines 'cause' for a funding termination under subsection (c)(2) as failure of an eligible entity to comply with agreement, State plan, or State requirements.
Correctly captures the discretionary authority granted to the Secretary in subsection (d) to prescribe effectiveness assessment procedures.
Accurately reflects the first clause of subsection (e)(1) permitting the chief executive officer of each State to revise any plan prepared under section 9908.
Accurately reflects the mandatory second clause of subsection (e)(1) requiring submission of any revised plan to the Secretary.
Accurately reflects subsection (e)(2) requiring public inspection of plans and revised plans within the State to facilitate review and comment.
Correctly captures the transitional rule under subsection (f) for fiscal year 2000 requiring application and plan submission under prior law rather than subsections (a)-(c).
